conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLA: Checked: EO 9385 only adds foreign food procurement functions to the Administration (an amendment), and EO 10945 sec. 5(a)(5) supersedes only the export-control provisions of EO 9380; neither is the ending. The ending is EO 9630 Part I para. 1, which terminates the Foreign Economic Administration itself, the entity every operative paragraph of EO 9380 runs through.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 9380 (8 FR 13081, Sept. 25, 1943; the held extract also carries neighbouring orders and a contents page): para. 1 establishes the Foreign Economic Administration (FEA) in the Office for Emergency Management; para. 2 consolidates four offices and the functions transferred by EO 9361 into it; para. 3 lets the Administrator create units; para. 4 makes its functions run in conformity with State Department foreign policy and, as military operations permit, gives it control of liberated-area supply and procurement; para. 5 transfers personnel, property and funds; para. 6 bars use of Public Law 139 funds abroad by the Administrator except as approved by the War Mobilization Committee; para. 7 amends conflicting prior orders and makes the order effective on the Administrator taking office. No own term. I read the held text of EO 9630 (10 FR 12245, Sept. 27, 1945), Part I para. 1: 'The Foreign Economic Administration established by Executive Order No. 9380 of September 25, 1943 ... and its agencies except as otherwise provided in this order, and the office of the Administrator of the Foreign Economic Administration, are terminated and disposition shall be made of the affairs thereof according to the provisions of this Part.' Paras. 2-6 then transfer its functions to State (incl. the liberated-areas function of EO 9380 para. 4, para. 2(c)), RFC, Commerce and Agriculture; para. 13 sets transfer dates no later than Dec. 31, 1945; para. 12 keeps prior regulations and directives relating to transferred functions in effect, which preserves administrative actions but not EO 9380 as an operating order. Every operative paragraph of EO 9380 (1-6) runs through the FEA or the Administrator, so termination of the FEA ends the whole order, as with Bowditch's EO 9204. EO 9380 is not named as revoked; the ending is the termination of the entity it created. D6 self-check: later events in the history are EO 9385 (Oct. 6, 1943, adds food functions; I read it, an amendment before the ending), EO 9630 (the ending), and the catalog 'See' to EO 9361 (an earlier order). EO 9630 was itself amended by EO 9730/9731 (para. 8 of Part II, State Department personnel sentence) and EO 9919 (export-control delegation to Commerce), and EO 10945 (May 24, 1961) sec. 5(a)(5)-(6) supersedes export-control provisions of EO 9380 and EO 9630; none of these restores the FEA or mentions reviving EO 9380 (I grepped FEA/9380 in all of them). No own term ran out earlier. Residual: para. 7's amendments of conflicting prior orders are executed text changes in other orders, not a continuing norm of EO 9380. Provisional NO hypothesis.
